rationales.F: DMS replicates databases and is not the intended public ingestion endpoint for application click events.

questions.central_requirement: Replayable ingestion, stateful stream transformation, and buffered analytics delivery to S3.
questions.decisive_words: retained for replay, stateful windows, continuous buffered delivery
questions.reusable_rule: Separate streaming pipelines into an ingest log, a stateful processing layer, and a managed delivery sink.

questions.stem: After a data-center migration, an enterprise will store hundreds of millions of long-lived objects in S3. Access patterns are unpredictable and can change over time. Objects must remain available with millisecond access, and the company wants automatic movement among access tiers without writing lifecycle predictions for each dataset. Which storage class is the best fit?

options.A: S3 Glacier Deep Archive for every object immediately after upload, submitting a restore request whenever access is needed.
options.B: S3 Intelligent-Tiering using its automatic millisecond-access tiers.
options.C: S3 One Zone-IA for the only copy of every irreplaceable object.
options.D: Amazon EBS io2 volumes attached permanently to one archive server.

rationales.A: Deep Archive requires asynchronous restoration and therefore cannot satisfy the millisecond-access requirement for all objects.
rationales.B: Intelligent-Tiering monitors access and automatically moves objects among eligible tiers while its immediate-access tiers retain millisecond access.
rationales.C: One Zone-IA stores data in one Availability Zone and is unsuitable as the sole copy of irreplaceable enterprise data.
rationales.D: Provisioned block volumes on a permanent server add capacity management and are not cost-effective at this object scale.

questions.central_requirement: Automatically optimize unpredictable S3 access patterns while retaining immediate object access.
questions.decisive_words: unpredictable, change over time, millisecond, automatic
questions.reusable_rule: Use S3 Intelligent-Tiering when access patterns are unknown or changing and automatic tiering is worth the monitoring charge.

questions.stem: A fleet of general-purpose EC2 instances uses gp2 EBS volumes. Most volumes are large only because the applications need more baseline IOPS, not more capacity. The team wants to provision required size, IOPS, and throughput independently and reduce storage cost without changing to a specialized high-endurance workload. Which volume type should be evaluated?

options.A: S3 Glacier Flexible Retrieval mounted as an EC2 boot volume.
options.B: EBS Provisioned IOPS SSD io2 Block Express for every volume.
options.C: EC2 instance store as the only durable database storage.
options.D: EBS General Purpose SSD gp3.

rationales.A: S3 Glacier is object archival storage and cannot be mounted as an EC2 boot block volume.
rationales.B: io2 is intended for demanding, high-durability and high-IOPS workloads and may add unnecessary cost here.
rationales.C: Instance store is ephemeral and cannot replace durable EBS volumes for persistent application data.
rationales.D: gp3 separates volume size from provisioned IOPS and throughput and is the cost-focused general-purpose SSD generation.

questions.central_requirement: Lower general-purpose block cost while provisioning capacity, IOPS, and throughput independently.
questions.decisive_words: large only for IOPS, independently, reduce cost
questions.reusable_rule: Evaluate gp3 when gp2 volumes are oversized merely to obtain performance tied to capacity.

questions.stem: A shared Amazon EFS file system contains project directories that are active for several weeks and then are rarely opened. Applications must retain the same NFS namespace and should not be rewritten. Which configuration reduces storage cost with the least operational effort?

options.A: Increase provisioned throughput so inactive files are read faster.
options.B: Copy every inactive file manually to an EC2 instance store volume and maintain a redirect catalog for every application.
options.C: Configure EFS lifecycle management to transition inactive files to an EFS IA storage class.
options.D: Create one EBS volume and mount it concurrently from instances in every Region.

rationales.A: More throughput can increase cost and does not move cold files to a lower-cost storage tier.
rationales.B: Instance store is ephemeral and host-local; the manual copy and redirect catalog also violate the requirements for unchanged applications and minimal operations.
rationales.C: EFS lifecycle management moves inactive files to lower-cost EFS storage while preserving transparent file-system access.
rationales.D: EBS is not a cross-Region shared NFS file system and does not preserve the existing EFS namespace.

questions.central_requirement: Automatically lower the cost of inactive EFS files without changing application file access.
questions.decisive_words: rarely opened, same NFS namespace, least effort
questions.reusable_rule: Use EFS lifecycle management when files become inactive but applications must retain transparent access through EFS.

questions.stem: A solutions architect is comparing AWS storage classes for cost optimization. Which THREE statements correctly describe important cost or availability characteristics that should influence the choice?

options.A: S3 Standard-IA has retrieval charges and a minimum storage-duration charge.
options.B: S3 Intelligent-Tiering requires the architect to predict and manually move every object between its automatic tiers.
options.C: Every S3 object can transition immediately to any class without minimum-size or minimum-duration considerations.
options.D: S3 One Zone-IA stores data in a single Availability Zone and is best for re-creatable or secondary copies.
options.E: An EBS snapshot must remain attached to a running EC2 instance to preserve its data.
options.F: S3 Glacier Flexible Retrieval and Deep Archive generally require a restore process before archived data is accessed.

rationales.A: Standard-IA trades lower storage price for retrieval and minimum-duration considerations, which matter for short-lived or frequently read data.
rationales.B: Intelligent-Tiering automatically moves eligible objects based on observed access; manual prediction is not required for automatic tiers.
rationales.C: Some transitions and storage classes have minimum object-size or duration charging considerations that must be evaluated.
rationales.D: One Zone-IA uses one Availability Zone and therefore suits data that can be recreated or has another durable copy.
rationales.E: EBS snapshots are durable incremental backups stored independently of whether the source volume remains attached.
rationales.F: The archive storage classes use asynchronous retrieval workflows rather than immediate access to archived object data.

questions.central_requirement: Recognize storage-class pricing and retrieval trade-offs before selecting a lower-cost tier.
questions.decisive_words: cost, availability characteristics, influence choice
questions.reusable_rule: Storage cost decisions must include retrieval fees, minimum durations, restore latency, and failure-domain requirements, not price per GB alone.

questions.stem: An enterprise has a predictable baseline of compute spending for the next three years, but teams may change EC2 instance families, Regions, and the balance among EC2, Fargate, and Lambda. Which purchasing option provides a discount while preserving the greatest flexibility across these compute services?

options.A: Dedicated Hosts purchased independently for every Lambda function.
options.B: EC2 Instance Savings Plans tied to one instance family and Region.
options.C: Spot Instances as a guarantee that all baseline production capacity will always be available.
options.D: A Compute Savings Plan with an appropriate hourly commitment.

rationales.A: Lambda does not run on customer-purchased Dedicated Hosts, and this would not provide the requested cross-service flexibility.
rationales.B: EC2 Instance Savings Plans can offer discounts but provide less flexibility because they are tied to a family in a Region.
rationales.C: Spot capacity can be interrupted and should not be treated as a guaranteed baseline for all production workloads.
rationales.D: Compute Savings Plans can apply across EC2 instance families and Regions and to eligible Fargate and Lambda usage.

questions.central_requirement: Discount a stable compute baseline while retaining family, Region, and compute-service flexibility.
questions.decisive_words: three years, change families and Regions, EC2 Fargate Lambda
questions.reusable_rule: Choose Compute Savings Plans for broad compute flexibility; choose narrower commitments only when their constraints are acceptable.

questions.stem: A media company migrates a fault-tolerant rendering farm to EC2. Jobs are checkpointed and can resume after interruption. A small amount of capacity must always be available, but burst capacity should use the lowest-cost compatible instances across several families. Which design is MOST cost-effective?

options.A: Run the entire peak fleet as fixed On-Demand instances continuously.
options.B: Use an EC2 Auto Scaling mixed instances policy with an On-Demand base and diversified Spot capacity for bursts.
options.C: Purchase Dedicated Hosts for every possible peak instance and leave them idle.
options.D: Use one very large EC2 instance with no checkpoint recovery or queue.

rationales.A: Keeping peak On-Demand capacity running wastes spend during lower-demand periods.
rationales.B: A mixed instances policy preserves a baseline while diversified Spot capacity reduces cost for interruption-tolerant burst work.
rationales.C: Idle Dedicated Hosts impose high fixed cost and are unnecessary for a flexible rendering workload.
rationales.D: One large instance creates a scaling and failure bottleneck and does not exploit the workload's checkpoint tolerance.

questions.central_requirement: Maintain a reliable compute baseline and use low-cost interruptible capacity for resilient bursts.
questions.decisive_words: checkpointed, small always available, lowest-cost burst, several families
questions.reusable_rule: Blend an On-Demand baseline with diversified Spot capacity when queued or checkpointed work can tolerate interruptions.

questions.stem: A platform team suspects that many EC2 instances and ECS services are overprovisioned, but it must preserve performance. It wants recommendations derived from recent configuration and utilization metrics, including projected utilization for candidate sizes. Which service should the team use first?

options.A: AWS Compute Optimizer.
options.B: AWS Artifact.
options.C: Amazon Route 53 Resolver.
options.D: AWS CloudHSM.

rationales.A: Compute Optimizer analyzes configuration and utilization to produce rightsizing findings, recommendations, and projected utilization.
rationales.B: Artifact supplies AWS compliance documents and agreements, not resource utilization recommendations.
rationales.C: Route 53 Resolver provides DNS resolution features and does not analyze compute sizing.
rationales.D: CloudHSM provides dedicated cryptographic hardware and has no compute-rightsizing function.

questions.central_requirement: Evidence-based rightsizing recommendations that preserve workload performance.
questions.decisive_words: overprovisioned, utilization metrics, projected candidate sizes
questions.reusable_rule: Use Compute Optimizer for utilization-based rightsizing guidance, then validate the recommendation before changing production capacity.

questions.stem: A steady Amazon RDS for MySQL production database must remain Multi-AZ. Monitoring shows sustained CPU below 20%, the application is compatible with AWS Graviton database classes, and the company expects to run the database for three more years. Which THREE actions can reduce cost without removing the availability requirement?

options.A: Add multiple unused read replicas even though no read-scaling requirement exists.
options.B: Right-size the DB instance after validating memory, connections, latency, and peak utilization.
options.C: Evaluate an eligible Graviton-based DB instance class and performance-test the application.
options.D: Disable Multi-AZ even though the stated production availability requirement remains.
options.E: Purchase an appropriate RDS Reserved DB Instance commitment for the stable baseline.
options.F: Replace the relational database immediately with DynamoDB without assessing schema or access patterns.

rationales.A: Unused replicas add database and storage cost without satisfying a stated performance or resilience need.
rationales.B: Rightsizing can remove excess capacity, but the team must evaluate more than average CPU before reducing the class.
rationales.C: Compatible Graviton classes can improve price performance when application and engine behavior are validated.
rationales.D: Removing Multi-AZ violates the explicit availability requirement and is not an acceptable cost optimization.
rationales.E: A Reserved DB Instance can discount a predictable long-running RDS baseline without requiring Multi-AZ removal.
rationales.F: A database-type migration without access-pattern and schema analysis is high risk and not an automatic cost reduction.

questions.central_requirement: Reduce a stable RDS workload's cost while preserving required Multi-AZ availability.
questions.decisive_words: steady, Multi-AZ must remain, low utilization, three years
questions.reusable_rule: Cost-optimize stable databases through evidence-based rightsizing, price-performance classes, and commitments without violating availability requirements.

questions.stem: A new DynamoDB workload has unknown traffic levels and can experience sudden unpredictable peaks. The team wants to avoid capacity planning and pay for the requests that the application performs. Which capacity mode is the most appropriate initial choice?

options.A: An RDS Reserved DB Instance applied to the DynamoDB table.
options.B: Provisioned capacity fixed permanently at one read and one write unit.
options.C: DynamoDB on-demand capacity mode.
options.D: EC2 Spot capacity assigned as DynamoDB partitions.

rationales.A: RDS reservations apply to eligible relational database instances and cannot purchase DynamoDB table throughput.
rationales.B: A permanently minimal provisioned setting would throttle peaks and requires capacity planning or auto scaling.
rationales.C: On-demand mode automatically accommodates changing request rates and charges per request without throughput capacity planning.
rationales.D: DynamoDB is managed and does not expose table partitions as customer EC2 Spot capacity.

questions.central_requirement: Cost and scale a new DynamoDB workload with unpredictable request volume and no capacity planning.
questions.decisive_words: new, unknown traffic, sudden peaks, pay per request
questions.reusable_rule: Start with DynamoDB on-demand for unpredictable traffic; evaluate provisioned capacity when usage becomes sufficiently stable.

questions.stem: An Aurora PostgreSQL cluster is highly I/O intensive. Monthly analysis shows that I/O charges are a large and consistent portion of total database spend. The workload will continue at this level, and the team wants predictable pricing without paying per I/O operation. Which storage configuration should be evaluated?

options.A: Aurora Standard with additional unnecessary read replicas.
options.B: Aurora I/O-Optimized cluster storage configuration.
options.C: S3 Glacier Deep Archive as the live Aurora transaction volume.
options.D: An EC2 instance store volume manually attached to the Aurora writer.

rationales.A: Unused replicas add compute and storage cost and do not eliminate Standard configuration I/O charges.
rationales.B: Aurora I/O-Optimized removes read and write I/O charges and is intended for I/O-intensive workloads where that pricing is beneficial.
rationales.C: Glacier Deep Archive is object archival storage and cannot serve as Aurora's live transactional storage.
rationales.D: Aurora manages its distributed storage layer and cannot use a customer-attached instance store volume.

questions.central_requirement: Reduce and stabilize the database cost of a consistently I/O-intensive Aurora workload.
questions.decisive_words: highly I/O intensive, large consistent I/O charges, no per-operation
questions.reusable_rule: Compare Aurora I/O-Optimized with Standard using the workload's measured I/O share; do not select it by name alone.

questions.stem: After migrating an analytics fleet into private subnets, a company discovers that most NAT gateway data processing is caused by large transfers from EC2 to S3 in the same Region. The instances do not need the NAT path for S3. Which change will reduce network cost while preserving private connectivity?

options.A: Assign public IPv4 addresses to every analytics instance.
options.B: Move the S3 traffic through an additional public NAT gateway.
options.C: Send the S3 traffic through a Transit Gateway in another Region.
options.D: Create an S3 gateway endpoint and associate it with the private subnet route tables.

rationales.A: Public addresses add exposure and public IPv4 cost and are unnecessary for private S3 service access.
rationales.B: Another NAT gateway preserves or increases NAT processing cost instead of removing S3 traffic from the NAT path.
rationales.C: Cross-Region transit adds unnecessary processing and transfer cost and does not optimize same-Region S3 access.
rationales.D: An S3 gateway endpoint routes service traffic privately without NAT gateway hourly or data-processing charges for that path.

questions.central_requirement: Remove high-volume same-Region S3 traffic from an expensive NAT gateway path.
questions.decisive_words: most NAT processing, EC2 to S3, same Region
questions.reusable_rule: Inspect dominant NAT destinations and use gateway endpoints for S3 or DynamoDB when those private service paths fit.

questions.stem: A network cost review finds three major patterns: private instances reach S3 through NAT gateways, global users repeatedly download the same cacheable objects from regional origins, and application tiers make unnecessary cross-Availability Zone calls to cache nodes. Which THREE changes directly address these cost drivers?

options.A: Centralize all outbound traffic through one distant NAT gateway regardless of Availability Zone or resilience.
options.B: Provision a Direct Connect circuit for every individual internet user.
options.C: Route same-Region traffic through another AWS Region before reaching its destination.
options.D: Add S3 gateway endpoints and route eligible S3 traffic through them.
options.E: Use Amazon CloudFront to cache and deliver the repeatedly requested public objects.
options.F: Place cache capacity in the required Availability Zones and route clients to local cache nodes when the service supports it.

rationales.A: A distant single NAT can add cross-AZ charges and a failure dependency; cost cannot be evaluated without resilience and topology.
rationales.B: Direct Connect connects sites or networks and is not provisioned separately for public internet consumers.
rationales.C: An extra Region adds latency and inter-Region transfer cost without addressing the identified patterns.
rationales.D: Gateway endpoints remove eligible S3 traffic from NAT processing while preserving a private service path.
rationales.E: CloudFront serves cache hits near users and reduces repeated origin processing and data transfer from the regional origin.
rationales.F: Zonal cache placement and locality-aware routing can avoid unnecessary cross-AZ bytes for chatty application-cache traffic.

questions.central_requirement: Reduce NAT, repeated origin-delivery, and avoidable cross-AZ network charges.
questions.decisive_words: S3 through NAT, cacheable downloads, unnecessary cross-AZ
questions.reusable_rule: Optimize network cost hop by hop: remove avoidable NAT processing, cache repeated delivery, and preserve zonal locality where appropriate.

questions.stem: A company will exchange several terabytes of data every day between its primary data center and AWS for at least five years. The transfer rate is steady, predictable network performance is important, and the organization can complete carrier provisioning. Which connectivity option should be evaluated for long-term price and performance?

options.A: An appropriately sized AWS Direct Connect connection.
options.B: A separate AWS Client VPN endpoint for every server.
options.C: S3 Transfer Acceleration as the private routing protocol for all applications.
options.D: A public IPv4 address on every on-premises storage device.

rationales.A: Direct Connect is designed for sustained dedicated hybrid connectivity and can provide predictable performance and different transfer pricing.
rationales.B: Client VPN is a user remote-access service and is not an efficient foundation for steady data-center-scale transfer.
rationales.C: Transfer Acceleration applies to S3 object transfers and does not create a general private hybrid application network.
rationales.D: Public addresses do not provide dedicated performance and would expand exposure and address cost.

questions.central_requirement: Cost-effective, predictable long-term hybrid connectivity for sustained high data volume.
questions.decisive_words: terabytes daily, five years, steady, carrier provisioning
questions.reusable_rule: Evaluate Direct Connect for sustained high-volume hybrid traffic when provisioning lead time and fixed connectivity commitments are acceptable.
